“The Committee continues to expect that, with gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace, and labor market conditions will strengthen somewhat further.” Interpreting this through the policy-rule lens of Clarida, Galí, and Gertler and Taylor, the 25 bp hike alongside guidance that rates remain below the longer-run level reflects gradualism and interest-rate smoothing consistent with a positive, but cautious, outlook. The emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent target and “monitoring inflation developments closely” underscores expectations management central to inflation targeting (Svensson and Woodford), especially as market-based inflation compensation remains low. Implementation via IOER and ON RRP (Goodfriend) and the planned balance-sheet normalization signal normalization without an abrupt tightening, while low term premia and inflation compensation (Cochrane and Piazzesi; Ang and Piazzesi) temper the degree of optimism. Overall tone: mildly positive, not exuberant.
